results.text: L-type calcium channel blockade worsens glucose tolerance and β-cell function in C57BL6/J mice exposed to intermittent hypoxia. Intermittent hypoxemia (IH), a pathophysiologic consequence of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), adversely affects insulin sensitivity, insulin secretion, and glucose tolerance. Nifedipine, an L-type calcium channel blocker frequently used for the treatment of hypertension, can also impair insulin sensitivity and secretion.
